doctor.title: Health
doctor.description: The checks of hostashi doctor, for the server and each site. They only read the server and change nothing.

errors.forbidden: Only administrators can run the checks.
errors.agent_timeout: The checks took too long. Try again.
errors.agent_unavailable: The checks could not be run. Try again.

services.title: Services
services.description: The system services of the server and the sites. systemd restarts a crashed service on its own; each automatic restart is listed below.

events.crashRestart: Restarted by systemd after a crash
events.crashRestarts: Restarted by systemd {{n}} times after a crash
events.title: Recent events
events.none: No restarts, failures or actions in the last 30 days.

empty.problems: No problems. Every service is running.
empty.sitesFilter: No site service matches the filter.
empty.sites: No site has a service of its own.
empty.serverFilter: No server service matches the filter.

confirm.title: {{verb}} {{name}}?
confirm.mariadb: Every site that uses a local database stops working until MariaDB runs again.
confirm.fail2ban: Brute-force attempts are not blocked while it is stopped.
confirm.other: The service stays stopped until you start it again.

errors.unreachable: The panel could not reach the server. Try again.

system.title: System
system.description: The server's name, time zone and clock, and the panel's own address. A reboot stops every site until the server is back.

server.title: Server
server.rebootWaits: Updates wait for a reboot. The server never reboots by itself.
server.rebootWaitsPackages: Updates wait for a reboot: {{packages}}. The server never reboots by itself.

updates.title: Updates
updates.notSetUpHint: the installer sets them up on its next run
updates.on: Automatic updates are on. New Hostashi versions install with the next daily security updates.
updates.off: Automatic updates are off. New Hostashi versions wait for sudo apt upgrade.
updates.hintOn: unattended-upgrades installs new Hostashi versions with the daily security updates, after a copy of the panel database.
updates.hintOff: New Hostashi versions wait for sudo apt upgrade. Health and an email say when one is out.

hostname.label: Hostname
hostname.hint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens; a full name such as web2.example.org works too. The panel's address and the sites do not change.
hostname.cloudInit: cloud-init is installed: Hostashi tells it to keep this name at the next boot.

errors.chars: Use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, with dots between the parts.
errors.address: This looks like an address, not a name.

timezone.label: Time zone
timezone.hint: Type to search, for example Europe/Berlin.
timezone.unknown: The server does not know this time zone.
timezone.follows: The sites' cron jobs run by the new time at once. MariaDB uses it after its next restart on the Services page. PHP keeps its own date.timezone setting.

reboot.title: Reboot
reboot.text: Every site, the databases and this panel stop until the server has started again, usually within one or two minutes.
reboot.goingDownText: This page waits and reconnects by itself.
reboot.startingText: This page reconnects as soon as the panel answers.
reboot.lost: The panel has not answered for ten minutes.
reboot.lostText: Check the server in your hosting provider's console.

pools.title: Storage pools
pools.description: Where the home directories of the sites live. A site stays on the pool it was created on; new sites land on the default pool unless you pick another.

quota.unknown: Unknown while the volume is missing

pools.noUsage: No usage while the volume is not mounted.
pools.newNameHint: The path, the sites and their files stay where they are. Scripts and API calls that use the old name need the new one.

add.title: Add or remove a pool
add.text: A new pool is a mounted, empty ext4 or XFS volume with <code1>nosuid,nodev</code1> and an entry in <code2>/etc/fstab</code2>. Hostashi never formats or mounts disks, so this happens on the server as root:
add.remove: A pool can be removed when no site is on it and it is not the default.

nameErrors.chars: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter, at most 32 characters.
nameErrors.taken: Another pool already has this name.

firewall.title: Firewall
firewall.description: Ports 80 and 443 are always open for the sites. SSH, the panel and API tokens are open to everyone until you set an allowlist. fail2ban blocks addresses after too many failed logins.
firewall.portError: Port {{n}}: enter a port such as 3000 or a range such as 6000-6010.
firewall.off: Hostashi's firewall is off: the server was installed with --no-firewall.
firewall.offText: Use the firewall in front of the server (for example at your provider), and let only SSH, 80, 443 and the panel port through. Run the installer again without --no-firewall to manage the rules here.
firewall.yourAddress: Your address as the panel sees it: {{ip}}
firewall.rollsBack: Every change rolls back after {{seconds}} seconds unless it is confirmed. A firewall in front of the server (for example at your provider) still applies: open a port there too.
firewall.rolledBack: The last change was not confirmed in time and was rolled back.

waiting.title: Waiting for confirmation
waiting.ssh: The SSH allowlist changed. Open a new terminal now and log in over SSH. Keep the session you have open until the test works.
waiting.countdown: The rules roll back in {{seconds}} seconds unless you keep them.
waiting.checking: Checking that the panel still answers…

foreign.title: A change is waiting
foreign.text: Another browser made a change that waits for its confirmation. It rolls back in {{seconds}} seconds unless that browser keeps it.

allow.title: Allowlists
allow.hint: One IP address or CIDR range per line, IPv4 or IPv6. An empty list leaves the port open to everyone. A home connection often gets a new address overnight; a VPN or a fixed office address works better.
allow.addPanel: Add my address to the panel

firewall.otherWay: I reach the server another way (VPN, another address, the provider's console)
firewall.applyHint: Rolls back after {{seconds}} seconds unless it is confirmed.

errors.forbidden: Only administrators can change the firewall.
errors.not_pending: The change was no longer pending: it was rolled back. Check the rules and try again.
errors.agent_error: The firewall could not load the rules. The previous rules stay.
errors.agent_timeout: The firewall could not be reached. Try again.
errors.agent_unavailable: The firewall could not be reached. Try again.

blocked.title: Blocked addresses
blocked.intro: fail2ban blocks an address for a while after too many failed logins. A blocked address reaches neither the sites nor the panel, and after repeated blocks not SSH either. Unblock an address here when a customer or you were locked out by mistake; it is blocked again after new failed logins.
blocked.unblockText: {{address}} is unblocked in every jail at once: {{jails}}.
blocked.truncated: fail2ban blocks more addresses than the panel reads, so some are missing below.
blocked.truncatedText: The counters above are complete. Narrow the list with the filters, or use fail2ban-client on the server.
blocked.noMatch: No blocked address matches the filters.
blocked.emptyPage: No address on this page; {{total}} in all.

errors.forbidden: Only administrators can see and unblock addresses.
errors.fail2ban_unavailable: fail2ban does not answer, so nothing is blocked right now. Check the service under Services.
errors.invalid_argument: Enter an IP address, a part of one, or a range such as 203.0.113.0/24.
errors.not_banned: This address is no longer blocked.
errors.agent_timeout: fail2ban could not be reached. Try again.
errors.agent_unavailable: fail2ban could not be reached. Try again.

runtimes.title: Runtimes
runtimes.fixesEnd_one: Fixes end in 1 day. Move its sites to a newer version.
runtimes.fixesEnd_other: Fixes end in {{count}} days. Move its sites to a newer version.
runtimes.installFailed: The installation did not finish. The log shows why; you can try again.
runtimes.removeFailed: The removal did not finish. The log shows why; you can try again.

php.description: The distribution's PHP is always installed. More versions come from the sury.org repository and get their updates automatically; one that no site uses can be removed.
php.securityEnds_one: Security fixes end in 1 day. Move its sites to a newer version.
php.securityEnds_other: Security fixes end in {{count}} days. Move its sites to a newer version.
php.eolText: PHP {{version}} gets no security fixes from PHP since {{date}}. Install it only for an old application that cannot move yet, and plan the move.
php.eolTextNoDate: PHP {{version}} gets no security fixes from PHP any more. Install it only for an old application that cannot move yet, and plan the move.
php.removeText: No site runs on it. Its packages and settings are removed from the server; you can install it again later.
php.newerText_one: sury.org offers this version already. Support comes with a Hostashi update.
php.newerText_other: sury.org offers these versions already. Support comes with a Hostashi update.

errors.forbidden: Only administrators can install PHP versions.
errors.running: Another installation is still running. Wait until it is done.
errors.inUse: Sites still run on this version. Move them to another version first.
errors.timeout: The server did not answer. Try again in a moment.

node.description: The long-term support lines of Node.js, from the official nodejs.org builds. Hostashi checks every download against its pinned checksum; a Hostashi update brings newer releases.
node.removeText: No site runs on it. Its files under /opt/hostashi/node are deleted; you can install it again later.
node.footer: Apps of a site run on the version chosen on the site's Web tab. A version can be removed once no site uses it.

python.description: The supported lines of Python, from the CPython builds of python-build-standalone. Hostashi checks every download against its pinned checksum; a Hostashi update brings newer releases and rebuilds.
python.removeText: No site runs on it. Its files under /opt/hostashi/python are deleted; you can install it again later.
python.footer: A Python site runs on the version chosen in its app settings, from its own environment ~/.venv. A newer release or build of a line keeps the environments and restarts their apps. A version can be removed once no site uses it.
